To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human PRC complexes 2 (hPRC2) structure reveals how the PRC2 core complex is assembled, how it recognizes the H3K36me3 peptide substrate, and the mechanism of action for the first small molecule inhibitor of PRC2, C646, which has been shown to be a potent inhibitor of H3K27me3 in cancer cells.

(1) The structure of the human polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRCs2) complex reveals a novel architecture of the EED subunits, which are critical for PRC2 catalytic activity; (2) PRC2 binds the H3K36 peptide in a conformational switch that is critical for PRC1 recruitment; (3) The structure of PRC2 in complex with a small molecule inhibitor reveals a novel mechanism of inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of chemical biology and structural biology methods to study epigenetic enzymes.
the structure and function of human PRC2, and how to use this information to develop novel inhibitors of PRC2 for cancer therapy.
the development of new methods and tools for the synthesis and study of complex organic structures, with particular emphasis on the synthesis of biologically active natural and synthetic molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PRC2 structure is an important advance in our understanding of PRC2 biology and will be useful for the rational design of inhibitors targeting the catalytic activity.
these recent breakthroughs have significantly advanced our understanding of PRC2 biology, and will likely provide important guidance in the future design of PRC2 inhibitors for cancer therapy.
the structure of PRC2 bound to the H2K27 peptide and small molecules provides a foundation to design novel inhibitors of PRC2 and to further elucidate the mechanism of PRC2 catalysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of the human Prc2 complex bound to H3K27 tri-methylated peptide provides a structural basis for the mechanism of PRC2 catalysis and the molecular basis for PRC2 inhibition.
the PRC2 structure is a key step in the development of a new generation of PRC2 inhibitors.
the PRC2 structure is a platform for drug discovery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the H3K9 peptide is a competitive inhibitor for PRC2 catalysis.
the catalytic activity and inhibitor selectivity of PRC2 depend on the relative orientation of the EZH2 SET domain and SUZ12 WD40 domain.
small molecule inhibitors can target the catalytic activity by binding to the active site of the PRC complex.
